newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA official appointed Air Liberte boss.
newsitem.headline: BA official appointed Air Liberte boss.

text.p: The chairman of British Airways' French subsidiary TAT, Marc Rochet, was appointed chairman of the management board of Air Liberte, Air Liberte said on Monday.
The appointment effectively marks the takeover by British Airways in partnership with Banque Rivaud of the insolvent French carrier.
Air Liberte said in a statement that founder Lotfi Belhassine resigned on Monday and recommended that Rochet succeed him. The board agreed.
"Mr Marc Rochet said he was determined to work as hard as possible for the recovery of the company," it said.

The BA/Rivaud rescue plan, presented after Air Liberte went into receivership in September, aims to restore Air Liberte to break-even by 1999. BA would take a 70 percent stake and Rivaud 30 percent of the airline.
A French commercial court in Creteil is expected to make a formal ruling in early January.

Richard Branson's Virgin Express said earlier this month that it would not bid for Air Liberte. Other prospective bids by smaller players did not appear to have sufficient financial backing, according to court sources.
BA's TAT and Air Liberte have a combined 22 percent share of the French market. BA has said it planned to merge the airlines.
